title: Pricing the Reduction for Reversed Covered Days on a Resident Charge (Medicare Part A Skilled Nursing Facility Coverage)
content:
**Medicare Part A Skilled Nursing Facility Coverage.** The reduction for reversed covered days on a resident coinsurance charge applies to the resident's original coinsurance charge for the coverage's latest booked coinsurance block, that is, among the coverage's booked-days entries in the band of benefit days 21 through 100 the one whose last service date is the latest, and it prices the days of the uncertified-day reversal posted against that booked-days entry after the charge was posted, under that reversal's own reason.

**Record test.** The reduction for reversed covered days is worked out only for a lapse's block that passes this record test: its service month carries one booked-days entry in the band of benefit days 21 through 100; at most one such entry of the coverage has the last benefit day just before the lapse's block's first benefit day; the bed-hold records book at most one leave for its service month and take back none of that leave's held days; its booked-days entry carries at most one day reversal for each reason and none for a booking error; no hospital-day or leave-of-absence reversal on it covers a held night of that leave, and each such reversal counts every day of its span; an uncertified-day reversal on it counts every day of its span except the held nights and the hospital-day and leave-of-absence days inside the span; and, when the supplemental effective date falls after the lapse's block's first service date, the block before it either has a resident charge billing exactly 100, 50 or 25 percent of that charge's own days times its own daily rate, to within half a percentage point, or carries a secondary charge and no resident charge; and, when the resident's charge for the lapse's block stands, its day count equals the lapse's block's booked days less the days of every day reversal posted against its booked-days entry on or before the date that charge was posted; and the lapse's block's last service date falls in 2024 or later, and the charge's open balance is above nothing. The block before the lapse's block is the coverage's booked-days entry in the band of benefit days 21 through 100 whose last benefit day is the day before the lapse's block's first benefit day; its resident charge is the resident coinsurance charge posted for it that is not a rebill of a denied secondary share.

For a block that passes its record test, the resident coinsurance charge, the card payment, the rate-year correction, the reduction for reversed covered days and the bank draft each count the days before the supplemental effective date as their own policies state, and only for such a block; for every other block, the tier that sets the split is the one in effect on the days of service: a Medigap policy changes the split from the carrier's policy effective date and QMB protection from the first day of the month after the state's QMB determination, so days before the supplemental effective date keep the earlier split, and none of these five figures is priced for it.

**The reduction.**

1. The reduction for reversed covered days prices each reversed day at the daily rate the resident's charge records, and reversed days before the supplemental effective date take the earlier share of 100 percent.
2. The supplemental effective date the reduction for reversed covered days reads is the one recorded on the coverage; a coverage that records none has the tier on file in effect on every day of the lapse's block.
3. The reduction for reversed covered days counts the reversal's day count, and it never exceeds the charge's open balance, which is its amount less the payments and adjustments posted against it plus any returned payments.
4. The reversed days the reduction for reversed covered days counts before the supplemental effective date are first the days of the reversal's span before that date: all of the span when its last day falls before the date, the days from its first day up to the day before the date when the date falls after its first day and on or before its last, and none otherwise.
5. Each kind of day named below that lies inside that part of the span, and that the lapse therefore did not reverse, is taken off those days, never leaving fewer than none nor more than the reversal's day count; the reversal's other days fall from the date.
6. A day already reversed as a leave-of-absence day on the lapse's block is not a day the uncertified lapse reverses: the days of the leave-of-absence reversal that lie inside the reversal's span come off the lapse's days before the supplemental effective date, all of that overlap when its last day falls before the date, the overlap from its first day up to the day before the date when the date falls after its first day and on or before its last, and none otherwise or when there is no such record.
7. Reversed days the reduction for reversed covered days counts before the supplemental effective date take the earlier share; every other reversed day takes the resident share of the tier on file. The resident share of the tier on file is that tier's resident share percent in the cost-sharing split schedule. When the tier on file prohibits balance billing, as the QMB Medicaid Crossover tier does, the reduction for reversed covered days bills the resident nothing for any day on or after the tier's supplemental effective date, those days taking the tier's resident share of nothing, while days before that date keep the earlier split, QMB protection not reaching back before it.
8. The reduction for reversed covered days adds, over the days it counts, the daily rate times the share each day takes, divides the sum by 100 and rounds it half up to the cent once.

### Hypothetical worked example

The latest booked coinsurance block of a coverage in the Medigap Plan A or B tier (resident share 100 percent) carries an uncertified-day reversal of 4 days posted after the resident's charge; the charge records a daily rate of 217.00; no supplemental effective date is recorded.

| Input | Value |
|---|---|
| Reversed days counted | 4 |
| Days before the supplemental effective date | None |
| Daily rate times share, summed | 217.00 times 4 times 100, that is 86800 |
| Divided by 100, rounded half up once | 868.00 |
| Charge's open balance 1500.00 | Not exceeded — reduction **868.00** |
| Charge's open balance 610.00 instead | Capped — reduction **610.00** |
